page: Google Cloud Platform g1-small is a shared-core virtual machine instance categorized within the general-purpose family. It provides 1 virtual CPU running on an Intel Xeon processor clocked at 2.3 GHz with the x86_64 architecture. The underlying hardware allocates a shared physical core featuring 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.25 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 45 MB L3 cache. Memory is provisioned at 1.7 GB to 2.0 GB of RAM. The instance includes no attached local storage and operates with zero dedicated GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark measurements reflect the constraints of its fractional, shared-core profile. In computational tests, the instance recorded a single-core stress-ng score of 1076.89, placing it in the bottom 25 percent of tested systems. Multi-core stress-ng performance achieved the identical value due to the single vCPU allocation, placing it in the bottom 10 percent. PassMark CPU testing yielded a score of 1263.03, alongside an encryption score of 401.65 and an extended instructions score of 1074.03. Memory bandwidth testing logged 80.25 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 10.49 GB/sec for larger 256 MB uncached reads.

Throughput benchmarks demonstrate modest handling capacity for low-intensity services. Redis SET operations measured 0.59 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput reached 0.54 GB/sec. Lightweight LLM inference using a 135M parameter model yielded 95.99 tokens per second for prompt processing and 20.22 tokens per second for generation. With its constrained shared-core scheduling and minimal RAM allocation, the instance provides cost efficiency for low-footprint utility functions, basic development or test setups, small automation scripts, and low-traffic web services.
description: Google Cloud Platform g1-small is an entry-tier, shared-core virtual machine designed for basic computing tasks. It features 1 vCPU mapped to a shared Intel Xeon core operating at 2.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, supported by 1.7 GB to 2.0 GB of system memory. The configuration includes no local storage, no discrete GPUs, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Performance evaluations indicate entry-level capabilities, with a single-core stress-ng score of 1076.89, a PassMark CPU score of 1263.03, and uncached large-block read memory bandwidth of 10.49 GB/sec. Application testing reveals a Redis throughput of 0.59 million SET operations per second and 0.54 GB/sec for static web serving. Given its resource limits and shared compute model, g1-small serves as an economical choice for low-intensity background utilities, dev-test environments, automation bots, and lightweight microservices.
